### RETRIEVED CONTEXT (MITRE ATT&CK / BENIGN PROFILES)
#### Match 1 (Confidence: 0.95)
- **Technique:** Endpoint Denial of Service: Service Exhaustion Flood (HULK) (T1499.002)
- **Tactic:** Impact
- **Description:** Adversaries may attempt to cause a denial of service (DoS) by sending a high volume of network traffic directly to a target. This specific profile mimics the HULK (Http Unbearable Load King) tool, which generates unique HTTP requests to exhaust server resources and bypass caching.
- **Typical Pattern:** Massive volume of unique HTTP GET requests with randomized headers (User-Agent, Referer) to prevent server-side caching and exhaust the application pool.
- **Mitigation:** Filter Network Traffic, Network Intrusion Prevention
- **Reference:** https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1499/002/

#### Match 2 (Confidence: 0.95)
- **Technique:** Endpoint Denial of Service: Service Exhaustion Flood (Slowhttptest) (T1499.002)
- **Tactic:** Impact
- **Description:** Slowhttptest is a highly configurable tool that simulates some Application Layer Denial of Service attacks. It implements most common low-bandwidth Application Layer DoS attacks.
- **Typical Pattern:** Slowly sending HTTP headers or POST bodies to keep connections open as long as possible.
- **Mitigation:** Filter Network Traffic, Exploit Protection
- **Reference:** https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1499/002/

#### Match 3 (Confidence: 0.95)
- **Technique:** Brute Force: Password Guessing (FTP) (T1110.001)
- **Tactic:** Credential Access
- **Description:** Adversaries may use brute force techniques to attempt access to valid accounts by guessing passwords. This profile focuses on FTP services where numerous login attempts are made systematically.
- **Typical Pattern:** Frequent, rapid connection attempts to port 21, typically with small packet sizes representing repetitive USER and PASS commands.
- **Mitigation:** Account Use Policies, Filter Network Traffic
- **Reference:** https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1110/001/
